questions.question_text:
Write the $x$- and $y$-intercepts of the line shown.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}\begin{axis}[width=6cm,height=5.4cm,axis lines=middle,axis line style={-{Stealth}},xmin=-1,xmax=4,ymin=-2,ymax=7,xtick={-1,0,1,2,3,4},ytick={-2,0,2,4,6},grid=both,clip=false,scaled ticks=false,ticklabel style={font=\small,/pgf/number format/fixed},xlabel={$x$},ylabel={$y$}]\addplot[thick,<->,domain=-0.3:2.6,samples=2] {-3*x+6};\end{axis}\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

options.why: Swapped the x- and y-intercept values with each other.
Wrote each intercept with its coordinates in the wrong order.
Attached each axis crossing to the wrong intercept.

questions.solution_text:
The line crosses the $x$-axis at $x=2$ and the $y$-axis at $y=6$.
$x$-intercept: $(2,0)$
$y$-intercept: $(0,6)$

[/tikz]

options.why: Read a gridline point $(1,3)$ as if it were the intercepts.
Used the $y$-coordinate $3$ of the point $(1,3)$ for both intercept values instead of reading the axis crossings.
Assumed a line through the origin misses both axes.

questions.solution_text:

$x$-intercept: $(0,0)$
$y$-intercept: $(0,0)$
